checks.details: pure gas and pure ice stay put above and below saturation (3 draws)
supersaturation deposits ice and undersaturation sublimates it (3 draws)
at saturation phi_t = -M dF/dphi with M > 0, so F decreases (3 draws, phi = 0.3 and 0.7)

relaxation: M*(-6*eps*gamma*(Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (x, 2)) + Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (y, 2)) + Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (z, 2))) + 6*gamma*(1 - 2*phi(x, y, z, t))*(1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*phi(x, y, z, t)/eps)
driving force: -alpha*(1 - phi(x, y, z, t))**2*(rho_v(x, y, z, t) - rho_vs(T(x, y, z, t)))*phi(x, y, z, t)**2

relaxation: - 3*M*eps*(Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (x, 2)) + Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (y, 2)) + Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (z, 2))) + 3*M/eps*phi(x, y, z, t)*(1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*(1 - 2*phi(x, y, z, t))
driving force: -alpha/rho_i*phi(x, y, z, t)**2*(1 - phi(x, y, z, t))**2*(rho_v(x, y, z, t) - rho_vs(T(x, y, z, t)))

agent's symbols.name: M
agent's symbols.meaning: Allen-Cahn interface mobility: how fast the diffuse interface relaxes toward the minimum of F (curvature-driven motion and profile restoration), taken constant

agent's symbols.name: alpha
agent's symbols.meaning: deposition/sublimation kinetic coefficient: rate of change of the ice fraction per unit vapor-density excess at the interface; it absorbs 1/\rho_i and the interface kinetics (sticking coefficient, molecular speed, 1/interface width), taken constant

agent's symbols.name: f
agent's symbols.meaning: bulk double-well density of F, f = 3\gamma/\varepsilon\,\phi^2(1-\phi)^2

agent's symbols.name: mu
agent's symbols.meaning: variational derivative \delta F/\delta\phi (chemical potential of the phase field)

agent's symbols.name: g
agent's symbols.meaning: interface indicator weighting the source, g = \phi^2(1-\phi)^2

agent's symbols.name: phi0
agent's symbols.meaning: equilibrium flat-interface profile along the normal coordinate X

agent's symbols.name: X
agent's symbols.meaning: coordinate normal to a flat interface

agent left out.why: The relaxation term $-M\mu$ already produces curvature-driven motion. The explicit shift $\rho_{vs}\,2\gamma v_m/(\kappa_B T r)$ is about $10^{-2}$ for $r\sim 0.1\,\mu$m and smaller for larger pores.
Kept constant for simplicity. They can be promoted to $M(\phi,T)$ and $\alpha(\phi,T)$ without changing the structure of the equation.

agent left out.effect: Anisotropy of $\gamma$ and of the attachment kinetics (facets)
agent left out.why: Ice basal and prismatic surface energies differ by only a few percent. The model is isotropic.
Grains are not part of this two-phase model; they would enter as boundary conditions or a third phase.

agent left out.effect: Density change, mechanical stress and flow of ice
agent left out.why: Ice is rigid at about 200 K on the time scales of interest. Stress energy is small compared with $\gamma/\varepsilon$.
$\kappa_B T$ is much smaller than $\gamma\varepsilon^2$ for $\varepsilon$ above about 1 nm, so fluctuations are negligible.

agent left out.effect: Coupling of the source to the vapor and heat equations (mass sink, latent heat)
agent left out.why: Not neglected physically. It belongs to the separate $\rho_v$ and $T$ tasks, since here $\rho_v$ and $T$ are given fields.
